subject: Medilabs - ephemeral retention acceptance criteria & proofwork template
messages:
From: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@medilabs.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Baker <tom.baker@medilabs.com>, security@medilabs.com
Date: Mon, 5 Jul 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on ephemeral retention / acceptable proof for SIG

Hi Stephanie —

Thanks for the demo last week. Our security team ran through Redwood's SIG responses and we have a follow-up: for ephemeral inference artifacts (prefix cache, transient KV traces, and debug sampling) we need clear acceptance criteria and a "proofwork" artifact that demonstrates deletion and retention behavior for SOC 2 review.

Specifically:
- What concrete artifacts can Redwood provide to show ephemeral data was treated as "non-persistent" (e.g., deletion timestamps, overwrite logs, or signed attestations)?
- For customer-specific exceptions (we may need to retain short windows for debugging), how would the exception be scoped, approved, and evidenced?
- Can you provide a template for the proofwork we should expect to collect for our auditor?

I've attached a short list of SIG questions (medilabs-sig-questions.pdf) and our auditor's checklist. Happy to hop on a call if easier.

Best,
Elena Martinez
Head of InfoSec, Medilabs
elena.martinez@medilabs.com

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@medilabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 6 Jul 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on ephemeral retention / acceptable proof for SIG

Hi Elena —

Thanks, and great questions. Looping in Ben (account lead), Kimberly (security/compliance), and Priyom (platform/product) so we can give you a single, auditable response and a repeatable proofwork template.

Quick answers up-front: we can provide (1) a proofwork template you can use for auditors, (2) signed attestations from our compliance team for standard ephemeral behavior, and (3) scoped exception flows for short-term retention with explicit approvers and TTL metadata.

Ben/Kim/Priyom — can you help with the specific evidence types (logs, signed deletion receipts, API call traces) and confirm what we can deliver within 5 business days? I sketched an approach below and welcome edits.

Proposed deliverables:
- Ephemeral proofwork template (spreadsheet) that maps each evidence item to SIG/SOC2 control clauses.
- Example deletion log (anonymized) showing timestamped KV purge and prefix-cache eviction.
- Signed attestation (.pdf) from Redwood Compliance for our default ephemeral retention behavior (30s-5m depending on model/route).
- Exception workflow doc: how to request, TTL override limits, approval chain, and a forensic snapshot handoff checklist.

Elena — would you prefer the artifacts as a Drive folder or as a packaged zip?

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Solutions - Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2027 10:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on ephemeral retention / acceptable proof for SIG

Folks —

I ran a quick intake with the account playbook. For Medilabs I recommend we:
1) Provide the proofwork template (attached: ephemeral-proofwork-template.xlsx).
2) Deliver a redacted sample log showing a KV purge run and the signed deletion receipt format (attached sample-kv-retention-log.txt).
3) Offer a one-hour evidence walkthrough with their auditor (we do these all the time).

Notes on exception scoping: our policy allows customer-requested short-term retention for debugging, but it must be:
- Requested via a formal ticket (we can accept their internal ticket ID or HubSpot).
- Limited to a maximum of 72 hours unless escalated to Security and Legal.
- Implemented as an auditable TTL override with a recorded approver and rationale.

Kim — can you draft the attestation language? Priyom — can you validate what fields we can include in the deletion receipt (signed hash, timestamp, job id, model route)?

Ben
Enterprise Sales Lead

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@medilabs.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 9 Jul 2027 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on ephemeral retention / acceptable proof for SIG

Hi Elena, Stephanie —

Attached is the attestation draft and the proofwork template (we also uploaded a copy to the shared Drive link below). High level:

What we can provide now (deliverable set):
- Proofwork template (spreadsheet) that maps evidence to SIG/SOC2 controls and indicates whether the evidence is generated automatically or requires a manual step.
- Redacted sample of deletion logs: includes job_id, deletion_timestamp (ISO8601), resource_type (kv_cache/prefix_cache), and redaction of tenant IDs.
- Signed attestation (.pdf) from Redwood Compliance describing default ephemeral policy and exception governance (attached).
- Exception flow playbook: ticket => Security review => TTL override with 2 approvers => automatic revert and deletion confirmation.

We will not include raw tenants or PII in sample logs; everything will be redacted per our data handling policy.

Next steps: I will finalize the attestation PDF and upload the pack to the Drive folder. Can your auditor confirm that a redacted deletion log + signed attestation + proofwork mapping table is sufficient for the SOC 2 control they are evaluating? If so, we'll package and share by EOD Monday (12 Jul).

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

From: Tom Baker <tom.baker@medilabs.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@medilabs.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on ephemeral retention / acceptable proof for SIG

Kimberly/Stephanie/Team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear scope. Our auditor confirmed that the package you described should be sufficient: redacted deletion logs, the attestation PDF, and the mapping table. They asked for the Drive link and an availability window for the walkthrough; we propose Tue 13 Jul 10:00am PT.

Can you confirm you can share the Drive folder link and the walkthrough seat (we expect one auditor + Elena)? If you can confirm by EOD today, we'll lock the slot.

Appreciate it.
Tom Baker
Security Operations, Medilabs
